note: Adds 'even for a moment' (ولو لحظة) not in source; omits the idea of the holy thing 'being swallowed' (כבלע).
Arabic makes Balaam the speaker ('Balaam said to him'), whereas source has God speaking to Balaam.
Adds 'great slaughter' not in source; omits the 'hip on thigh' detail.
Arabic adds negation: 'do you not know' instead of 'do you know'.
Reverses meaning: source says death WILL separate me and you; Arabic says 'if anything other than death separates'.
Arabic says 'Yahweh has a god in Israel' instead of 'there is God in Israel' — meaning changed
Changes 'we are like ten thousand' to 'you equal ten thousand of us' — subject/person shifted from we to you.
Arabic says 'my way' where source has 'his way'.
Arabic adds causal 'because she lay upon him' instead of 'the night on which she lay upon him'.
Adds 'rest of the house' and 'holy of holies', not in the source.
Adds 'and at the end of that year' before Samaria was captured, which is not in the source.
Adds 'part of' to the hundred of silver, changing the amount; also omits the entreaty 'we pray'.
Adds the vocative 'O God' not present in the source.
Omits the idea 'as polluted/defiled' (וַיְגֹאֲלוּ); only 'excluded from the priesthood' is given.
Adds 'before my face' (أمام وجهي), which is not in the source.
Arabic makes 'I am wicked' conditional ('if I am guilty'), changing assertion to hypothesis.
Arabic says 'who does not know such things' instead of 'who does not have such things'.
Renders 'until he fulfills his day' as 'until he is happy in his day,' changing the predicate's meaning.
Changes third-person 'he has made me weary' to second person 'you,' and turns the question 'have you destroyed' into a statement.
Statement 'They are like stubble' turned into a question 'Will they be...?'
Passive 'the arms of the fatherless are crushed' rendered as active 'you crushed', adding God as agent.
Changes 'his words' to 'his deeds' and adds 'in all your words'; source says he does not answer any of his words.
Arabic singular object 'restrain him/it' instead of source plural 'them'.
Second clause changed from statement ('he will be swallowed up') to question ('will he be swallowed?').
Omits 'lightning' (חֲזִיז), rendering only 'voice of thunder'.
Renders 'appetite' as 'life' and changes lion/young lions to lioness/cubs of lionesses.
Adds clause 'and make his face be broken' not in the source
Renders 'do not fret' as 'do not be deceived,' changing the exhortation's idea.
Adds 'the East' (الشرق); source מִקֶּדֶם means 'of old/ancient times', not east.
Adds 'you said' and quotation, turning the statement 'you are my refuge' into God's speech; changes speaker.
Omits the source idea 'from fat/oil' (מִשָּׁמֶן) as the cause of the body's wasting.
Second clause says 'quarrels with all sound wisdom' instead of 'will be overthrown in every enterprise'.
Arabic says cease hearing instruction so you will not stray; source says instruction leads to straying from knowledge.
Adds second-person 'You who send'; replaces 'meted out and trodden under foot' with 'strong, victorious'.
"You made me serve" (הֶעֱבַדְתַּנִי) rendered as "you wearied me", losing the serving/enslaving idea.
Omits the clause 'I would comfort myself' concerning sorrow.
'I have drawn you with kindness' rendered as 'I prolonged mercy for you'—the idea of drawing is replaced.
Omits the clause 'as if it were a very little thing' (כמעט קט); 'بل' replaces it.
Adds 'good' and changes 'mix the mixture' to 'cook the broth'.
Adds 'Egypt' as object of 'draw' ('draw Egypt'), not in source, which says 'draw it' (the sword).
Arabic uses second person 'you eat/strip/break/spread' instead of third person 'they' of the source.
Adds 'في الخارج' (outside) at the end, not present in the source.
Arabic says thieves and swearers are acquitted/cleared, reversing source 'shall be cut off'; also adds 'false' to swearer.
Adds clause 'and people heard of him' not in the source, which only says the report went out.
Adds 'to it' (Caesarea): Festus was about to depart shortly, not go to Caesarea.
Adds 'والنعمة' (and grace/blessing), a distinct idea not in the source's 'thanks be to God'.
Adds 'نعمة' (grace), a distinct idea not in the source, which has only joy and comfort.
Arabic adds 'الرسالة' (the message) alongside 'the promise'; source has only one noun.
